In [[mathematics]], '''Nakayama's conjecture''' is a [[conjecture]] about [[Artinian ring]]s, introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Nakayama|authorlink=Tadasi Nakayama|year=1958}}. The '''generalized Nakayama conjecture''' is an extension to more general [[ring (mathematics)|ring]]s, introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Auslander|last2=Reiten|year=1975}}. {{harvtxt|Leuschke|Huneke|2004}} [[mathematical proof|proved]] some cases of the generalized Nakayama conjecture.

Nakayama's conjecture states that if all the [[module (mathematics)|module]]s of a minimal [[injective resolution]] of an [[Artin algebra]] ''R'' are [[injective module|injective]] and [[projective module|projective]], then ''R'' is [[self-injective ring|self-injective]].
